_what: The last round of bibliographic metadata for the four submission-form manuscripts: the entries that carried a bare PMCID, a bare author name, or a title fragment and no identifier at all.
_why: These were reported as 'needs another fetch round' and left as a caveat. Reading the actual entries rather than the summary showed all but one were resolvable now - six bare PMCIDs, three exact titles and two author-plus-disease pairs.
⚠_this_query_returned_unrelated_papers_a: The two AUTH-keyed clauses pulled in papers by the same authors on other diseases - peritoneal mesothelioma (37400148), intramuscular myxomas (28160572), retroperitoneal leiomyoma (25875009) and a commentary on the proteome map (25925092). An author query is a retrieval, not an identification. Each entry below was matched to its manuscript reference by title, not by proximity in the result set.
⛔_one_entry_could_not_be_identified_and_: Surface-target reference 16 reads 'Sjögren H, et al. EWSR1/NR4A3 fusion in extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma'. Three Sjögren papers on this disease returned and NONE matches: 10537274 is a TAF15 (TAF2N) fusion, 11156374 is a TCF12 fusion, 12598313 is a cytogenetics and microarray study. None is an EWSR1-fusion paper. The entry is also UNCITED in the body text, so no context disambiguates it. All three candidates are recorded in the manuscript entry; it must be resolved or removed by a human, never completed by picking the nearest.
⛔_a_second_entry_is_incomplete_at_the_so: PMC2395470 / PMID 18521326 (Sarcoma 2001;5(Suppl 1):S37-43) returns an EMPTY author string and a title of only 'Biology', a supplement section heading. Europe PMC itself holds no author list for it. Resolve against the printed supplement.
⚠_eight_references_in_the_surface_target: Refs 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 have no in-text citation marker - measured by counting every [n] in the file, which runs 1-8 plus 11 and 12. Almost certainly the cut from 11,740 to 4,553 words removed the citing sentences and left the entries. A journal will reject an uncited reference list. Not fixed here: deciding whether to restore the text or drop the references is an authorial call.
